title: AI Cluster Ethernet RoCEv2 Load Balancing & Congestion Control Selection Benchmark (256xH100 400G Leaf-Spine)

provenance.notes: All throughput, tail latency, PFC pause rate, and monthly TCO figures are generated by a deterministic analytical hash-collision and queueing simulator calibrated to published 400G RoCEv2 (50.0 GB/s per NIC), Broadcom Tomahawk 5 DLB/Cognitive Routing, and NVIDIA Spectrum-X / ConnectX-7/8 Out-of-Order RDMA specifications. No paid cloud or physical 256-GPU Leaf-Spine switch cluster was spun up in this session.

ecmp_pfc_dcqcn.label: Option A: Standard 5-Tuple Static ECMP + PFC + DCQCN (1 QP/peer)
ecmp_pfc_dcqcn.hardware_dependency: Standard RoCEv2 Leaf-Spine switches + any RoCEv2 NIC (in-order RDMA only)

ecmp_qp_scaling.label: Option B: Static ECMP + Multi-QP Scaling (4 QPs/peer) + ECN/DCQCN Tuning
ecmp_qp_scaling.hardware_dependency: Zero hardware change; env tuning (NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=4, NCCL_IB_SPLIT_DATA_ON_QPS=1)

flowlet_dlb.label: Option C: Switch Dynamic Load Balancing (DLB / Flowlet Switching) + In-Order RoCEv2
flowlet_dlb.hardware_dependency: DLB-capable Leaf-Spine switches (e.g., Broadcom Tomahawk 4/5) + standard in-order RoCEv2 NICs

packet_spraying_ooo_rdma.label: Option D: Per-Packet Adaptive Spraying + NIC Hardware Out-of-Order (OoO) Direct Data Placement
packet_spraying_ooo_rdma.hardware_dependency: Adaptive Packet-Spraying Switch + OoO-capable RDMA NIC (Spectrum-X / Tomahawk 5 + ConnectX-7/8 / UEC)

architect_takeaways: 1. Why Standard 5-Tuple Static ECMP Collapses on AI Traffic: Unlike web traffic with millions of short TCP flows, AI training (NCCL Ring/Tree AllReduce) generates a small number of massive 400G elephant flows per GPU rail. Deterministic 5-tuple hashing maps multiple 400G flows onto the same Spine uplink (2.20x oversubscription while neighboring links sit idle), triggering PFC pause storms (14.8% pause rate) and dropping effective fabric utilization to 54.0% (27.0 GB/s = 216.0 Gbps AllReduce busbw, 78.4% cluster goodput).

2. Zero-Cost Day-1 Remediation on Existing Switches (Multi-QP Scaling): Setting NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=4 and NCCL_IB_SPLIT_DATA_ON_QPS=1 splits each GPU-pair elephant flow across 4 Queue Pairs with distinct UDP source ports, raising 5-tuple hash entropy and lifting 256-GPU AllReduce busbw by 1.37x (27.0 -> 37.0 GB/s = 296.0 Gbps) and cutting MoE All-to-All P99 latency from 42.0 ms to 26.5 ms (1.58x) with zero hardware cost (saving $75,014.55/month).

3. Switch Flowlet DLB vs. Per-Packet Spraying + Hardware OoO RDMA: On standard in-order RoCEv2 NICs, enabling Switch Dynamic Load Balancing (Flowlet Switching on Tomahawk 4/5) achieves 85.0% fabric utilization (42.5 GB/s = 340.0 Gbps, 1.57x vs Static ECMP) without out-of-order retransmission drops; for >=256-GPU clusters and MoE All-to-All workloads, pairing Adaptive Per-Packet Spraying with NIC Hardware Out-of-Order Direct Data Placement (Spectrum-X / Tomahawk 5 + ConnectX-7/8 / UEC) reaches 95.0% fabric utilization (47.5 GB/s = 380.0 Gbps, 1.76x), slashes MoE All-to-All P99 latency by 3.75x (42.0 -> 11.2 ms), lifts cluster goodput to 98.2% (+19.8 pts), and recovers $145,616.49/month.
